## Observation

Driving `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0` through rebar's agentic runner on Bedrock fails before any request is sent. Reproduced on main 6dbf05538f7 with the pinned `pydantic-ai-slim` 1.107.9 and a scripted Converse client: `PydanticAIRunner(cfg).run(RunRequest(..., execution_mode="agentic"))` raises `LLMUnavailableError: the LLM provider call failed: bedrock_supports_strict_tool_definition`.

## Root cause (measured)

- pydantic-ai's `BedrockConverseModel._map_tool_definition` (models/bedrock.py:519 in 1.107.9) reads `self.profile.bedrock_supports_strict_tool_definition` directly whenever a tool definition is `strict`.
- `BedrockProvider.model_profile` returns a `BedrockModelProfile` for every vendor prefix except `meta` (and unknown vendors, which return `None`): `meta` maps to `_without_builtin_tools(meta_model_profile(...))`, a plain `ModelProfile`. Surveyed all 11 vendor prefixes plus an unknown one: only `meta` and the unknown case lack the field. `ModelProfile.__getattr__` raises `AttributeError(name)`, which the runner surfaces as the bare field name.
- Upstream defect. pydantic-ai main now reads `self.profile.get('bedrock_supports_strict_tool_definition', False)`; the latest 1.x release (1.107.10) still has the direct read, and rebar pins `>=1.107,<2`. So rebar must work around it.
- rebar builds the provider in `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.build_bedrock_provider`; pydantic-ai resolves the model's profile from `provider.model_profile`, so that is the seam (rebar already overrides `model_profile` the same way for its OpenAI-compatible provider in `providers.py`).

## Approach

1. In `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py`, return a `BedrockProvider` subclass whose `model_profile(name)` returns `BedrockModelProfile.from_profile(upstream or DEFAULT_PROFILE)`. For a profile that is already a `BedrockModelProfile`, `from_profile` returns an equal object (checked for anthropic, qwen, openai), so every other vendor is unchanged; for `meta` and unknown vendors it adds the Bedrock fields with their upstream defaults (`bedrock_supports_strict_tool_definition=False`), so a strict tool is sent without `strict`, as pydantic-ai main does.
2. A comment names the upstream defect and the 2.x fix so the subclass can be removed on the 2.x upgrade.
No config key, env var or flag.

## Capability classification (measured)

`capabilities._capabilities_from_profile` sets `prompt_cache_style="bedrock"` when the profile exposes `bedrock_supports_prompt_caching`; its comment states the intent: a Bedrock-hosted model is `bedrock` style "regardless of family". Today meta is `none` only because of the same upstream gap. After the wrap, meta's capabilities equal amazon.nova-pro's shape (`bedrock` style, `native_structured_output=False`); mistral and cohere are also `bedrock` style without caching. `capabilities.py` is not edited. The 2 consumers of the `bedrock` style, checked:
- `cache_settings_for` returns `bedrock_cache_instructions`/`bedrock_cache_tool_definitions`/`bedrock_cache_messages`. pydantic-ai 1.107.9 applies each only when the profile's `bedrock_supports_prompt_caching`/`bedrock_supports_tool_caching` is True (models/bedrock.py 894-895, 928, 1102-1103, 1117-1118); both default False for meta, so no `cachePoint` is sent.
- `structured.native_output_stack_supported` is called only under `caps.native_structured_output` (structured.py:162-163), which is False for meta, so output routing is unchanged.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py`
- `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py`

## Testing

- RED then GREEN: the agentic runner, with a scripted Converse client (the `test_sampling_opt_in.py` pattern), completes a turn for `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0`; on the pre-fix tree it raises `LLMUnavailableError` naming `bedrock_supports_strict_tool_definition`.
- A tool-using turn: the script returns a `toolUse` for an agentic tool, then `end_turn`; the run completes and the second Converse call carries the `toolResult`.
- Classification: after the fix a meta model's capabilities are `bedrock` style with `native_structured_output=False`, and the agentic Converse request for meta (instructions + tools) carries no `cachePoint` block.
- For every vendor prefix `BedrockProvider.model_profile` knows (anthropic, mistral, cohere, amazon, meta, deepseek, openai, qwen, google, minimax, nvidia) plus an unknown one, the built provider's `model_profile` is a `BedrockModelProfile`, and for vendors whose upstream profile already is one it equals upstream.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A test that fails on the pre-fix tree reproduces the error for a `us.meta.*` model through the agentic runner.
- [ ] The root cause is recorded on this ticket with evidence (upstream 1.x defect, rebar-side workaround).
- [ ] The agentic runner completes a tool-using turn for `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0` in a test.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live agentic probe of `us.meta.llama4-maverick-17b-instruct-v1:0` on Bedrock completes, recorded as a comment.
  provenance: environment=Bedrock us-west-2 via the frontier-bedrock profile from the fix-seal worktree; principal=frontier-bedrock IAM identity; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — one agentic run with a tool turn
- [ ] A test shows a meta model is classified `bedrock` style with no native structured output, and its agentic Converse request carries no `cachePoint`.
- [ ] Every Bedrock vendor prefix resolves to a `BedrockModelProfile`; profiles that already were one are unchanged.
- [ ] [non-codebase] `env -u JIRA_URL -u JIRA_USER -u JIRA_API_TOKEN make verify` exits 0 on the commit pushed for review.
  provenance: environment=macOS dev host, fix-seal worktree; principal=Rebar Bot Nava; privilege_posture=narrower; instrument=live-call — exit status and log live outside the repository
